entries.name: Available to promise
entries.purpose: The stock LN can still promise to a new order, worked out period by period, and the extra check on components and capacity when that stock falls short.
entries.explanation: Stock on the shelf is not what LN promises. Planning works out, period by period, how much of an item is still free once later demand has its share, and checks a new order against that. When the free stock falls short, it can go on to ask whether the missing components and capacity can be found in time. So an order can be refused while the stock is plainly on the shelf.

entries.name: Backorder
entries.purpose: The part of a sales order line that the final delivery did not ship, which waits to be confirmed and then becomes a new line to deliver.
entries.explanation: When the final delivery of a sales order line ships less than was ordered, the rest is not lost and not shipped on its own. It waits as a backorder. Once someone confirms it, or a parameter does so by itself, it becomes a new line to deliver. Left unconfirmed, it's goods a customer is waiting for that nobody plans to ship.

entries.name: Business partner
entries.purpose: Any party you trade with, where customer and supplier are two roles on one partner and not two separate records.
entries.explanation: LN keeps one record for every party you trade with, and gives it roles. Customer and supplier are two roles on one partner, not two lists. The roles carry defaults, so an order type or office that looks wrong on an order is usually right for the partner chosen. A missing role fails only when an order needs it, such as a purchased item with no supplier to buy it from.

entries.name: Contract deliverable
entries.purpose: A second way to raise demand on an item, beside a sales order, which planning ignores until it is switched on and whose supply stays tied to its project.
entries.explanation: A contract deliverable raises demand on an item for a project, beside the sales orders. Unlike a sales order, planning ignores it until someone switches it on, and nothing warns that it is waiting. Once it is planned, its supply is held for that project, so stock made for it is not free to sell.

entries.name: Embedded GenAI
entries.purpose: LN's built-in AI. A prompt written once by an administrator, sent with LN data to the Infor GenAI service, and run as a command on a screen.
entries.explanation: Embedded GenAI is a question someone prepares once and attaches to a screen. An administrator writes the prompt, chooses the LN data that goes with it, and links it to a session. Users then see it as a command on that screen, and it answers about the record in front of them. The answer comes from the Infor GenAI service, not from LN, so the data sent with the prompt is what to review.

entries.name: Installed base
entries.purpose: What Service knows about the equipment it looks after: serialized items, their physical breakdown, and the installation groups they are kept in.
entries.explanation: Service tracks equipment one unit at a time. Each unit is a serialized item with a lifetime serial number, which can be built from other serialized items in a physical breakdown. Units at one place for one owner form an installation group. Contracts, warranties, maintenance plans and service orders all point at these.

entries.name: Maintenance sales order
entries.purpose: The order for repairing a customer's part in your own shop, and the work order that does the repair.
entries.explanation: In depot repair the customer sends a part in, it is repaired in your shop, and it goes back. The maintenance sales order is the customer side, what comes in, what goes out and what is charged. The work order is the shop side, the activities, labor and material of the repair. A part maintenance line links the two; the work order can also stand alone.

entries.name: Non-conformance report
entries.purpose: The record of material or work that does not meet its requirement, how it is reviewed, and what is decided about it.
entries.explanation: A non-conformance report, or NCMR, records something that failed: a rejected quantity at an operation, a rejected receipt, a failed test, or a deviation found at a supplier. A review board or owner decides what happens to it, such as scrap, return to vendor, use as is or no fault found. The decision is carried out on the quarantined stock, which makes the adjustment or return order.

entries.name: Order planning
entries.purpose: LN's name for what most people call MRP. It lives in the package called Enterprise Planning, beside master planning, which is LN's name for MPS.
entries.explanation: Order planning is LN's name for what most people call MRP, and it sits in the package called Enterprise Planning. It compares demand with stock and open supply, and proposes planned orders to cover the gap. The run does the same thing every time, so when an item is not planned, or planned oddly, the answer is almost always in that item's planning or ordering data.

entries.name: Order type
entries.purpose: A code on an order that carries the procedure the order will follow, so changing it changes how the same order behaves.
entries.explanation: An order type is a code on an order that decides the procedure it follows, not a label for reports. In Warehousing it sets which steps LN runs for you and which are yours. Two orders for the same item can need different steps because their types differ. So when one order has a step another doesn't, check its order type first.

entries.name: Planned order
entries.purpose: Planning's proposal to buy or make something, which becomes a real order only when it is transferred and can be thrown away until then.
entries.explanation: A planned order is planning's proposal to buy or make something, and nothing outside planning knows about it. It becomes a real purchase or production order only when it is transferred. Until then the next planning run may throw it away and propose something else. That is why planning can be rerun freely, and why a planned order number isn't an order number.

entries.name: Project contract
entries.purpose: How a customer project is split in two in LN Project: the contract holds what is sold and how it is invoiced, the project holds the work, its budget and its costs.
entries.explanation: In LN Project a customer order becomes two linked things. The contract says what the customer pays and when, line by line. The project says what work is done, what it should cost and what it did cost. Each contract line is linked to the project's elements or activities, and the project cannot start until that link and the contract are active.

entries.name: Release
entries.purpose: LN's verb for handing an order from one module to the next. It changes a status and unblocks the next step, and it moves no goods.
entries.explanation: Release is LN's word for handing an order from one module to the next. A sales order is released to Warehousing, a production order to the job shop, and outbound advice so that picking can start. Each changes a status and unblocks the next step, and none of them moves goods. After a release, the warehousing order is the document to read.

entries.name: Scenario
entries.purpose: One complete planning answer. Every planning screen is scoped by one, and only the actual scenario is real.
entries.explanation: A scenario is one complete planning answer. Every planning screen is scoped by one, and planners can keep others to compare options, but only the actual scenario is real. When a plan and an order disagree, the first question is which scenario the plan is in.

entries.name: Service contract
entries.purpose: A sales agreement to look after a customer's equipment for a period, saying what is covered, how service costs are covered, and how the contract is invoiced.
entries.explanation: A service contract says which of the customer's equipment is looked after, for how long, what the service costs it covers, and what the customer pays for it. Service orders and calls on covered equipment check it, so covered costs are charged to the contract instead of invoiced. The contract itself is invoiced in installments, and its revenue can be spread over its periods.

entries.name: Service order
entries.purpose: The order for service work at the customer's site or in the company: activities, engineers, material, hours and costs, through to invoicing.
entries.explanation: A service order plans and records repair or maintenance work on a customer's equipment, usually at their site. It comes from a service call, preventive maintenance, a field change order, a project or by hand. Its activities get engineers and material, the engineers report hours and material, and costing the order sends its costs to invoicing, checked against any contract or warranty.

entries.name: Session
entries.purpose: Infor's word for a screen. Each has a code, shown in the status bar, that names it exactly.
entries.explanation: A session is Infor's word for a screen. Each has a code, shown in the status bar, that names it exactly, while its name can differ between the menu, the help and the screen. The code is the stable way to say which screen you mean.

entries.name: Shipment and load
entries.purpose: What leaves the warehouse together. LN groups picked lines into a shipment and shipments into a load by itself, and reads each one's status from the lines under it.
entries.explanation: LN groups what leaves the warehouse by itself. Each picked order line becomes a shipment line, lines going the same way share a shipment, and shipments that travel together make a load. Their status follows the lines under them, so a shipment that won't move on is waiting for one of its lines.

entries.name: Site and warehouse
entries.purpose: Four things often taken for one: a warehouse is where goods are stored, a site is a business location, an enterprise unit is the part of the organization that does the accounting, and a planning cluster is what planning works on.
entries.explanation: These are four words a newcomer hears as one. A warehouse is where goods are stored, and a site is a business location with its own logistic data. An enterprise unit is a part of the organization that accounts for itself, and a planning cluster is what planning works on. An item can be missing from any of them, and LN shows no error for it.

entries.name: Warehousing order
entries.purpose: The order that controls every movement of goods in a warehouse. Most are generated by sales, purchase and production orders, and a transfer is entered by hand.
entries.explanation: Every movement of goods in a warehouse is controlled by a warehousing order. Sales, purchase and production orders each cause one to be made, and a transfer is entered as one by hand. After an order is released, its warehousing order shows what the warehouse has done about it.

entries.name: Warehousing procedure
entries.purpose: The list of steps an order takes through the warehouse, each one run by LN or left to you, which is why advice, pick, freeze and confirm do not always apply.
entries.explanation: A warehousing procedure lists the steps an order takes through the warehouse, such as advice, release, pick, freeze and confirm. Each step is set to be run by LN or left to you. That is why the same flow needs a manual step on one order and none on another, and the order's activity table says which.

entries.name: Warranty
entries.purpose: The guarantee that a part is repaired free or for less within a period, set up once and checked by calls, service orders and maintenance sales orders.
entries.explanation: A warranty says what repair costs are covered, and for how long, after a unit is delivered or put into use. It is set up as a template with coverage terms and linked to a service item, so each serialized item of it gets its own copy when delivered. Calls, service orders and maintenance sales orders then check it, and covered costs are charged to the warranty instead of the customer.

entries.name: WIP
entries.purpose: The value a production order has taken in and not yet delivered. Issuing material or posting hours books it, and the first booking makes the order Active.
entries.explanation: Work in process is the value a production order has taken in and not yet delivered. Issuing material or posting hours books it, and the first booking makes the order Active. So Active means cost is on the order, and changing a status won't undo it.
